headline: Claude 在黑洞物理上解出两个开放问题，AI 正从写代码工具变成基础科学的生产工具

overview_bullets.text: Claude 解出黑洞物理两个开放问题登顶 HN，这是今天唯一一条 AI 直接产出硬科学成果的信号，比任何榜单排名都更值得记。
GitHub 趋势榜被 Claude Code 技能包刷屏——BugHunter、superpowers、diagram-design、stitch-skills，智能体的竞争焦点已从模型能力转向可复用的技能资产。
Gemini 4 Neon 登上 Models Engineering Index 第一，但热度仅 57.8，说明榜单公信力与社区关注度正在脱钩。
Anthropic 七位创始人 IPO 各套现 2.8 亿美元、公司募资近 1050 亿，AI 头部实验室的估值已进入兑现期而非投入期。
法院裁定第四修正案禁止使用 AI 生成的『合理依据』，同时 PostgreSQL 19 因 AI 报漏洞潮推迟两个月发布——AI 的双刃剑同时砍向司法与基础设施。

executive_summary: 今天的信号很清晰：AI 的价值正从『能聊』转向『能干活』，而它干活的地方既有黑洞物理，也有漏洞报告和法庭证据，前者是红利，后者是代价。

editor_note.core: 今天最该记住的是 Claude 解出黑洞物理开放问题——它证明大模型在形式化推理密集的领域已能产出可验证的新知识，这比任何 benchmark 排名都更能定义这一年的技术水位。
editor_note.cross_signal: 开源侧的技能包爆发（BugHunter 的 82 个技能、superpowers 的方法论框架）与 Apple 招聘自研智能体、Gemini 4 Neon 登顶榜单相互印证：智能体的瓶颈已不在模型本身，而在技能封装与工程化落地。
editor_note.counterintuitive: Gemini 4 Neon 拿到 Models Engineering Index 第一却只有 57.8 热度，而一个 Claude 技能包能到 72.6——社区用脚投票表明，能直接干活的工具比榜单名次更有价值。
editor_note.risk: PostgreSQL 19 因 AI 报漏洞潮推迟两个月发布，加上法院禁止 AI 生成『合理依据』，说明 AI 大规模生成内容正在给安全审计与司法系统制造噪声成本，这部分代价目前没有任何一方在计账。

contradictions: 一边是 AI 在黑洞物理等前沿科学上产出可信成果，一边是法院明确禁止 AI 生成的『合理依据』进入司法程序，同一技术在不同领域的可信度被截然分割。
Anthropic 创始人 IPO 套现近 2B 美元，而开源社区最热的项目是免费分发的 Claude 技能包，价值捕获与价值创造出现明显错位。
Gemini 4 Neon 被评为工程指数第一，但社区热度远低于多个 Claude 技能仓库，榜单权威性与实际采用度不一致。

comments.one_liner: firecrawl 是一个面向 AI agent 的知识基础设施，通过单一 API 提供搜索、抓取以及接入 550 多家数据源的能力
comments.why: 把抓取、搜索和 550+ 数据源统一到一个 API，意味着 agent 的数据接入层从各家自建爬虫转向标准化采购，中小团队的数据工程成本被压到接近零。
comments.stance: 数据获取正变成水电煤，护城河从『能抓到』转移到『抓得干净且合规』。

comments.one_liner: 一个 AI agent skill，可跨 Reddit、X、YouTube、HN、Polymarket 和网页检索任意话题并汇总成有据可依的摘要
comments.why: 把跨平台检索与摘要合成打包成一个可复用技能，意味着 agent 的信息搜集从单站抓取转向多源交叉验证，直接压缩人工调研的时间成本。
comments.stance: 多源聚合是 agent 技能里最实用的一类，但摘要的可靠性取决于源质量，别把它当事实核查工具。

comments.one_liner: obra/superpowers 是一套面向 AI agent 的技能框架与软件开发方法论
comments.why: 把 agent 技能封装成可复用的方法论框架，等于给『提示词工程』补上工程规范，团队协作时技能可以像依赖包一样被版本化和审查。
comments.stance: 技能框架会像当年的 lint 规则一样成为标配，不采用的一方会在多人协作中先乱。

comments.one_liner: 一个 Claude Code 漏洞挖掘技能包，含 82 个 skills、15 个 slash 命令和 681 条已披露报告模式
comments.why: 把 681 条已披露报告模式固化成技能包，让外部红队工作从个人经验变成可复制的检索库，攻击面知识扩散速度加快。
comments.stance: 攻防知识的技能化不可避免，防守方必须假设对手已拥有同等清单。

comments.one_liner: 一套面向 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等 AI 编程工具的编辑级图表设计资源，涵盖 45 种图表类型，输出自包含的 HTML 与 SVG
comments.why: 针对多个 AI 编程工具输出自包含 HTML+SVG 图表，直接绕开 Mermaid 的渲染限制与样式失控，让 AI 生成的图能进正式文档而非草稿。
comments.stance: 『No Mermaid slop』是正确宣战：图表质量是 AI 产出能否交付的分水岭。

comments.one_liner: Ghost-Downloader-3 是一款开源的多功能下载器桌面应用
comments.why: 下载器把多协议、多源聚合进单一客户端，用户不再为不同站点装不同工具，边缘工具类软件的整合窗口正在关闭。
comments.stance: 集大成者往往也是最后一款——这类工具的价值在于终结选择困难，而非创新。

comments.one_liner: AFFiNE 是一个开源、隐私优先的知识库工具，把文档、白板与规划功能整合在一起
comments.why: 把文档、白板、规划合并进一个隐私优先的开源知识库，直接对 Notion+Miro 的组合收费模式施压，企业采购多了一个可自托管的替代项。
comments.stance: 开源替代的胜负手不在功能对齐，而在迁移成本——这一步它还没证明。

comments.one_liner: 一份开源的上架合规手册与提交前检查工具，收录 117 种 App Store 与 Google Play 拒审模式及修复方案，并提供面向 AI 编程 agent 的技能
comments.why: 把 117 条被拒模式和 95 个监管截止日做成预提交检查，等于把应用商店审核与合规风险前移到编码阶段，AI agent 也能直接调用。
comments.stance: 合规检查下沉到开发工具链是必然，晚做的团队会用一次下架来补课。

comments.one_liner: Google Labs 的 Agent Skills 库，配合 Stitch MCP server 使用，遵循 Agent Skills 开放标准
comments.why: 官方按 Agent Skills 开放标准发布技能库并绑定自家 MCP 服务，等于用兼容性换生态入口，其他编码 agent 也被纳入其分发路径。
comments.stance: 标准兼容是聪明的渠道策略，但技能库若只服务于自家 MCP，开放标准就只是包装。

comments.one_liner: AutoClip 是一款开源 AI 视频剪辑桌面工具，能把播客、访谈、课程等长视频自动剪成适配抖音、小红书、TikTok 等平台的短视频
comments.why: 长视频自动切片、字幕、封面、文案一条龙且开源本地运行，把原本外包给剪辑师的短视频产能交回创作者手里，内容分发的边际成本被再次压低。
comments.stance: 切片工具会迅速同质化，真正的差异在选题判断，不在剪辑速度。

comments.one_liner: Onlook 是 YC W25 推出的开源桌面工具，在真实代码库之上叠加画布，让设计师直接借助 AI agent 在代码中做设计
comments.why: 在真实代码库上叠画布、让设计师直接改代码，压缩了设计稿到实现的交接环节，设计工具的竞争从画布转向对代码库的理解能力。
comments.stance: 方向对，但设计师改代码的信任门槛远高于工具门槛，采用曲线会比宣传慢。

comments.one_liner: 有报告称 Claude 解决了黑洞物理学中的两个开放问题
comments.why: 若模型能推进黑洞物理的开放问题，说明 AI 在形式化推理上的产出开始进入同行评议范畴，科研评价与署名规则会被迫跟进。
comments.stance: 单点成果不等于科研范式转移，但审稿人从此必须假定投稿背后有模型。

comments.one_liner: 一篇研究论文，提出基于前一个 token 预测的 LLM 反演方法，用于还原模型的输入提示词
comments.why: 基于下一 token 预测反推提示词，意味着系统提示与私有上下文可被从输出侧还原，提示词保密作为防护手段的有效性被直接削弱。
comments.stance: 把提示词当商业秘密的团队该醒：泄露路径在输出端，不在输入端。

comments.one_liner: 一个基于 WebGPU 的浏览器端交互式演示，展示如何用 LLM 检查并修改 Qwen3.5-0.8B 的权重，仅改动 0.016% 的参数
comments.why: 把权重编辑从需要多卡显存的实验室流程压进浏览器单页，让个人开发者也能在本地对开源小模型做定向行为改写并即时验证效果。
comments.stance: 降低门槛的方向正确，但只改 0.016% 权重就能稳定改变行为，也意味着模型后门与审查式微调更难被外部察觉。

comments.one_liner: Gemini 4 Neon 登上 Models Engineering Index 榜首
comments.why: 榜单头名易主会直接改写企业选型时的默认候选，并迫使其他厂商在工程可用性而非跑分上重新对标。
comments.stance: 单一工程榜单的排名波动被当成行业定论，是当下模型评估最脆弱的一环。

comments.one_liner: 美国空军少校 Jason Watson 已被单独监禁近 100 天
comments.why: 现役军官被长期单独关押且细节稀缺，会把军内司法程序与羁押透明度推到公众审视之下，牵动同僚与家属的处境。
comments.stance: 近百日单独关押在任何制度下都需要公开的法定理由，沉默本身就是问题。

comments.one_liner: 法院裁定第四修正案不允许使用 AI 生成的「合理依据」
comments.why: 法院把算法生成的推断排除出合理根据，等于要求执法机关为机器结论提供可质证的人工依据，直接影响依赖此类工具的搜查与立案流程。
comments.stance: 这是必要的一刀：不可交叉质询的机器判断不能成为剥夺人身自由的门票。

comments.one_liner: 航空订票、银行与生产力平台接连出现故障，安全专家认为背后可能有更深层原因
comments.why: 航空、银行、办公平台接连故障被指向自动化运维与智能体链路，意味着单点错误会沿依赖链放大成跨行业同时停摆。
comments.stance: 把智能体接进关键系统却不做降级与熔断设计，是在用用户的时间替厂商做压力测试。

comments.one_liner: Anthropic 七位创始人在创纪录的 IPO 中合计套现近 20 亿美元
comments.why: 创始团队在上市首日套现近二十亿美元，把公司治理重心从长期使命转向股价与锁定期，也重塑员工期权与后续融资的定价基准。
comments.stance: 安全叙事与巨额退出同时成立时，外界有权追问谁的激励还绑在风险控制上。

comments.one_liner: Linear COO Cristina Cordova 讲述公司如何将 GTM 体系扩展至 1 亿美元 ARR
comments.why: 把一款工具型产品做到上亿美元经常性收入并公开拆解销售与运营路径，为同类 SaaS 提供了可复用的增长参照，也暴露工具类产品的天花板争议。
comments.stance: 这类复盘比融资新闻有用得多，但个案成功被当成通用公式是行业最常见的误读。

comments.one_liner: Apple 正招聘工程师打造自家 AI agent，可浏览网页、跨应用操作、写代码并调用服务
comments.why: 苹果自建可跨应用操作、能写代码和调用服务的智能体，会把系统级权限变成竞争壁垒，第三方应用的分发与入口地位随之被重新分配。
comments.stance: 平台方亲自做代理层，等于既当裁判又当选手，开放接口的承诺需要被持续盯住。

comments.one_liner: 回顾 Nvidia 近期股价波动的来龙去脉
comments.why: 股价剧烈波动叠加管理层临时代班，说明市场对算力需求的定价已从增长故事转向对订单可持续性的怀疑，波及整条供应链的估值。
comments.stance: 把单季财报电话会当成信仰确认仪式的人，正在为下一轮回撤付学费。

comments.one_liner: Meta 新款 AI 可穿戴设备 Muse Charm 售价可能为 300 美元
comments.why: 三百美元价位的 AI 可穿戴若成真，会把常驻摄像头与麦克风推向大众消费级，隐私边界与社交场合的接受度随之被重新谈判。
comments.stance: 价格下探不是进步本身，先给出可验证的录制提示与数据留存规则再谈普及。

comments.one_liner: PostgreSQL 19 正式发布，比往年 9 月的惯例晚了两个月，主要原因是团队需处理大量由 AI 报告的漏洞问题。
comments.why: 发布节奏从九月惯例推迟两个月，直接原因是 AI 辅助漏洞挖掘把补丁队列压到团队处理能力上限，这意味着数据库这类基础组件的升级窗口从此要按安全事件而非日历排期。
comments.stance: 延迟本身不是问题，把 AI 挖洞带来的漏洞洪流当成新常态、并让发布流程为它让路，才是这一版真正的信号。

it_222a3317cded8e05.title: Scaling Linear’s GTM to $100M ARR — Cristina Cordova, COO
it_222a3317cded8e05.summary: Open video on YouTube ↗ Linear was founded to build a better issue tracker. Seven years and $134 million in funding later, its CEO Karri Saarinen published a post titled "Issue tracking is dead." In this episode, we chat with Cristina Cordova , COO of Linear , about how the company navigated that and how its go-to-market changed along the way. Cristina spent seven and a half years at Stripe, led platform and partnerships at Notion, and was a partner at First Round before joining Linear in 2023. Linear's founders built it after living with legacy issue trackers at Coinbase, Airbnb and Uber, and it spread self-serve through startups like Vercel and Ramp. When she joined, Linear had about 40 people and one salesperson. Since then it has shipped an MCP server, a platform for building agents into Linear, integrations with Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and its own Linear Agent. Agents created 3% of Linear's work a year ago. Now it's more than half. Linear passed $100 million in ARR this year with more than 40,000 paying customers and 177% net revenue retention, and in August employees sold $99 million in stock at a $2.5 billion valuation . We talk about why she stopped chasing enterprise deals three weeks after joining, why Linear has never hired a single SDR, why it won't let an LLM answer support tickets on its own, and what the AI budgets behind $100M-in-months ARR mean for everyone else. Half the work on Linear is now created by agents Linear shipped its MCP server in May 2025, and Cristina says it was basically the first in its category. A year and a half later, more than half the issues created in Linear come from agents. That doesn't mean Linear wants to be a database with an MCP server on top. Cristina thinks SaaS companies settling for that are making a big mistake. If the agent workflows inside your product aren't better than the ones outside it, nobody has a reason to open your app. So she watches two lines: agent usage and app usage. If agent usage climbs and app usage doesn't, you're becoming a commodity. At Linear, both are up and to the right, because people still come back to the app to see and coordinate the work. Jump to the MCP discussion → "Issue tracking is dead" When Karri published "Issue tracking is dead" in March, most of Linear's customers agreed with him. Then they asked the obvious question: so what am I buying? Linear's answer is a product development system built around agent orchestration, where humans stop doing the manual work of filing, labeling, assigning and closing issues. Customers had been pushing it there. Most of the frontier AI labs run on Linear and wanted it to move faster. Pre-AI companies like Ramp and Coinbase were building their own internal agents and needed an API to plug them into Linear. Cristina says Linear is lucky it's small enough to cannibalize itself. Google has a much harder problem: put an AI answer above every search result, and fewer people look at the ads. Jump to the "issue tracking is dead" discussion → The AI budget behind $100M in months The thing speeding up purchases right now, Cristina says, is AI budget. Companies carved out money for AI tools that didn't exist before, and any product that fits inside it skips the usual fight for spend. At some companies that budget is very high. It's already starting to change. Buyers are signing one-year deals and paid pilots, not three-year contracts, because nobody knows what they'll want in two years. And some overnight-$100M stories are a handful of $30 to $40 million contracts with defense companies or giant law firms. That's a very different business from Linear's 40,000 paying customers on what was, until June, entirely seat-based pricing. When those one-year deals come up for renewal, we'll find out whose ARR was real. Jump to the AI budget discussion → Linear threw out its 2025 enterprise roadmap Three weeks after joining in 2023, Cristina crossed "move upmarket to enterprise" off Linear's company goals. It had one salesperson. She went after growth-stage companies that would have to rip out an existing tool instead, the same way Stripe won new businesses long before it won switchers. Linear finally declared an enterprise push in 2025, with a roadmap full of features for large organizations. Then agents happened. Linear built an MCP server, an agents platform with a whole new set of APIs, and integrations with Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot. None of it was planned, and a lot of the enterprise work never got done. Cristina chose to race ahead anyway. Competitors waited, and enterprises started putting Linear on their shortlists. Jump to the enterprise roadmap discussion → No SDRs, no forward deployed engineers Linear has never hired a single SDR. Cristina thinks the qualification call wastes the customer's time: they want a demo, not questions about their budget. AEs do their own outbound, with tooling to keep it personal. It doesn't do forward deployed engineering either. Linear should be easy enough to adopt that nobody needs access to your systems. Solutions engineers sell alongside enterprise AEs instead, sometimes building a working ServiceNow integration overnight to show a prospect it can be done. Cristina adds that an opinionated tool gives agents cleaner data than one where every team defines "bug" differently. Support stays in-house, and Linear won't let an LLM answer tickets on its own. AI drafts replies and a human decides what goes out. Customers sometimes assume the replies are AI because they arrive so fast. In three and a half years, Cristina has never had an escalation over a bad support experience. Jump to the sales team discussion → Everyone wants outcome-based pricing Cristina would love a model like Intercom's Fin, which charges for each support conversation its AI resolves. It's harder for Linear. What is auto-triaging a bug to the right team worth when one company thinks that's the PM's job and another doesn't? Until someone cracks that, Linear charges for what costs it money and keeps the rest free. Seats stay. Linear Agent chat is free even though it runs on frontier models. In coding sessions, users pick OpenAI or Anthropic models and harnesses, and Linear passes through the published API price plus a small markup. Loops run on AI credits. Linear doesn't start charging for things that used to be free. New AI features launch as free betas with notice that pricing is coming, and prices start high and come down rather than the other way around. Jump to the pricing discussion → Why not hire 100 salespeople? Cristina says Linear runs on about half the headcount of companies at its stage and revenue. A sales team bigger than the rest of the company would have cost it the trust engineering now has in sales. From Stripe she brought a 40% rule: at least 40% of the company should be engineering, product, design and data. If sales wanted more people, it helped recruit engineers first. Linear has no hard rule, but one of the first things she built was a headcount spreadsheet by function, and she still watches the ratio. Hiring is slow on purpose. Candidates do a work trial on a real problem. Hers was writing Linear's go-to-market plan for the next six to twelve months, which then became her job. At about 170 people, the only C-suite is the founders and her. Jump to the hiring discussion → Show notes Linear — the product development system where Cristina is COO. Sharing Linear's growth with the people building it — the August tender at a $2.5 billion valuation, with more than 40,000 paying customers and 177% net revenue retention. Issue tracking is dead — Karri's March post on why Linear is building for agents. Linear MCP server — the May 2025 launch Cristina says was basically a first for the category. Introducing Linear Agent — the built-in agent whose chat Linear keeps free. How we built Triage Intelligence — the feature that suggests labels and catches duplicates in incoming issues, Cristina's example of AI that doesn't need to be an agent Coding sessions in Linear — the June launch that ended Linear's all-seat pricing, running Claude Code and Codex on AI credits. Introducing Loops — recurring agent jobs, also billed with AI credits. Intercom Fin pricing — $0.99 per resolved conversation, the outcome-based model Cristina wishes fit Linear. it_4ba1303d2ee21d77.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
it_4ba1303d2ee21d77.summary:
PostgreSQL 19 Released
Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse.
This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one:

For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary.

In practice, that looks like this:
UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama';
SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn();

That returns a value like 0/0306EE20 . Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do:
WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s');
SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama';

The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch up within the specified time.
I first encountered this pattern in Wikipedia , which has a hand-rolled version of this built against MySQL replication:

In addition to this, MediaWiki attempts to ensure that the user sees events occurring on the wiki in chronological order. A few seconds of lag can be tolerated, as long as the user sees a consistent picture from subsequent requests. This is done by saving the primary binlog position in the session, and then at the start of each request, waiting for the replica to catch up to that position before doing any reads from it.

Here's the relevant MediaWiki code , which these days uses MySQL's WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET() function and falls back to SOURCE_POS_WAIT() .
